title: Predictive kernel-aware pacing and priority batcher to reduce tail latency
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: mixed workloads (short chat turns + long context prefill requests + heterogeneous quantized model variants) cause kernel-switch churn and uneven batch shapes leading to elevated tail latencies (P99) on hosted and dedicated clusters.

Goal: design and ship a lightweight predictive admission + batch shaping layer that uses cheap runtime signals to: 1) prefer admission decisions that minimize kernel switches inside a batch, 2) pace low-priority/latency-tolerant decode work to smooth resource usage, and 3) apply priority-aging so small requests are not starved by long prefill jobs. Target: reduce P99 latency by >=15% on mixed workloads while keeping throughput loss <10%.
acceptance_criteria: Staging A/B (5% traffic) shows P99 reduction >= 12% for mixed workload replay vs baseline over 7 days
Token throughput (tokens/sec) regression < 10% and cost-per-token change documented
No customer-facing errors introduced; fallbacks disable predictor and revert to existing admission logic
Unit and integration tests for predictor, batch shaping rules, and priority-aging are merged
Design doc and rollout plan reviewed by Infra and Runtime leads
notes: High-level approach: derive a per-request kernel-affinity score from (model_variant, quantization_level, estimated_decode_length, recent-kv-state) and a fast cost model for kernel-switch overhead. Use a logistic predictor (few features) to estimate incremental latency impact if admitted immediately vs delayed by up to 50ms.

Why logistic predictor: NN predictors add inference overhead inside the admission path and can themselves become a source of jitter. A small linear+sigmoid model trained offline gives most of the benefit with near-zero runtime cost and easy introspection.

Batch shaping policy: prefer assembling batches homogeneous in kernel-affinity first (same quantization/kernel family). Allow 20% cross-affinity padding to avoid starvation. Implement a short-leash timer (5ms) to avoid holding small requests for long batching windows.

Priority/aging: requests have base priority (interactive>background>prefill). Apply exponential aging where waiting raises effective priority; cap aging at 200ms to bound starvation while avoiding oscillation.

Prefill vs decode scheduling: prefill requests that will produce large KV caches are given a warmup window to start earlier, but long decodes can be throttled if they would force kernel switches for many short requests. Add an explicit 'prefill-warm' flag used by routing to ensure customers with long-context workloads get KV warmed without blocking interactive lanes.
Fallbacks: predictor can be toggled per-cluster. For Dedicated customers with strict SLAs we default to deterministic admission (current path) unless customer opts-in.

Trade-offs considered: more aggressive grouping yields lower kernel-switch overhead but increases latency for low-priority requests; we bias toward safer defaults for hosted tier to protect PLG experience.
updates: 2024-11-22: Spike complete — collected 48h of production traces and labeled kernel-switch events. Identified 3 dominant kernel families (fp16, int8-ggml, ivfpq). Baseline P99 for mixed replay = 412ms.

2024-11-27: Prototype logistic predictor (5 features) implemented in Rust admission path; microbench shows <100ns median overhead per decision. Initial model trained on last-30d traces (GitHub dataset) and validated on replay traces; predicted delta correlates r=0.78 with observed latency impact.
2024-11-30: Batch shaping simulator run across 10k-request replay: predicted P99 down 19% but token throughput down 6%. Decision: conservative tuning for rollout (allow small cross-affinity padding).

2024-12-03: Design review with Runtime and Infra — approved with two action items: add observability hooks (per-request kernel-affinity tag) and canary control to ramp predictor on/off via feature-flag.
2024-12-05: Integration tests added (unit + e2e). Canary plan drafted: 2% -> 5% -> 20% over 10 days with health checks on P99, error rate, and GPU utilization.
next_steps: Merge PRs for predictor and batch controller; add feature-flag gating and observability tags (ETA 2 days)
Deploy canary to staging with 2% traffic and validate metrics for 48h
Run cost regression analysis; if >8% regression, iterate on padding and timer values
Post-mortem and rollout retrospective scheduled after 2-week canary
